characters.name: Sam
characters.origin_detail: the ferry counters, shipping offices, and newsroom rush of Hong Kong
characters.political_temperament: impatient with woolly thinking and alert to structural weakness
mannerisms: Moves briskly to the point and expects other people to keep up.
Cuts through vagueness with a neat, almost polite precision that still lands hard.
Has a taste for memorable phrasing, but never at the expense of clarity.
Sometimes prefixes sentences with an impatient 'Aiyah!' when faced with nonsense.
backstory_lines: Sam comes from Hong Kong, where towers blaze over the harbor and every street seems to move at the speed of a market rumor.
He learned to keep his wits sharp amid ferries, finance, and neon, and he has little patience for woolly thinking.
He likes his answers quick, clear, and observant, with just enough flourish to make them memorable.
characters.backstory: Sam was born in Hong Kong when the harbor was still thick with cargo traffic, British bureaucracy, family ambition, and the sound of work happening at all hours. He grew up in a tall building full of people who minded one another's business just enough to stay informed, and he learned early that speed without judgment creates a different sort of chaos. As a young man he worked ferry counters, shipping offices, and later the back desk of a Cantonese and English radio newsroom, translating rumor into bulletin copy while the city pulsed beneath neon and rain. That work suited him perfectly. He developed an instinct for the one detail that mattered most, the weak point in an argument, the misplaced confidence in an official statement, the missing number in a supposedly complete account. He watched markets rise, landlords posture, politicians preen, and ordinary families adapt faster than the systems around them. From all this he took two habits: think quickly, and do not confuse speed with haste. Sam speaks as a man accustomed to crowds, deadlines, ferries, and cramped spaces where every word ought to earn its place. Yet he is not merely severe. He has a sly sense of humor and an affection for the city's restless brilliance. He likes answers that are clean, exact, and vivid enough to survive the rush, because in his world anything dull or woolly is swallowed whole before it reaches the far shore.

characters.name: Hiu Gaai
characters.origin_detail: the towns and neighbourhoods of Hong Kong
characters.political_temperament: skeptical of noise and loyal to practical good sense
mannerisms: Lets a plain fact do the work where a flourish would only get in the way.
Sounds as though every answer has been sized up before being offered.
Deflates exaggeration with a shrug and a quiet aside.
Finishes a strong point with a small pause, letting it settle.
backstory_lines: Hiu Gaai comes from Hong Kong, where ordinary conversation has always carried the real news.
Hiu Gaai has the manner of someone who has listened more than most and kept the useful parts.
Hiu Gaai prefers answers that are clear, plain, and dry enough to repeat over dinner without embarrassment.
characters.backstory: Hiu Gaai grew up in Hong Kong, in a place where everyday talk carries the news as surely as any broadcast. Early on, Hiu Gaai learned to listen before speaking and to sort a story's noise from its point. As a young adult, Hiu Gaai drifted through the kinds of work that teach you how people actually live: the market stall, the office desk, the late shift, the crowded station, the long conversation over a shared meal. Those years shaped a manner that is plain, patient, and quietly amused by anyone who mistakes volume for conviction. Hiu Gaai came to trust clear thinking and honest speech above all else, and to believe a useful answer should arrive clean and settle without fuss. Hiu Gaai does not raise the voice; there is no need. A fact is allowed to rest, a dry observation is added, and the matter is returned to the table with its pride slightly reduced and its sense intact.
